name: pdh_pdl_fakeout_5s
author: adapted from QuantGen_Subagent_2
thesis: Previous Day High/Low are obvious technical levels where retail traders place stop losses. Institutional players often drive price just beyond these levels to trigger stops (liquidity hunt) before reversing. Exists due to predictable stop placement.
mechanism: Previous day's high/low are key reference levels where stop-losses and pending orders cluster. When price approaches these levels, two forces compete: breakout orders above/below and reversal traders fading the move. The resolution depends on volume — high-volume breaches trigger cascading stops, while low-volume approaches tend to reverse.
weaknesses: A True breakout with heavy volume will obliterate this strategy
Slippage can be high right at the liquidity sweep
Requires quick execution as the reversal happens rapidly
adaptation_notes: Converted from 15min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 180x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; stop/target recalibration for 5-second timeframe. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
